blocks.x: There is a plain version of conversational ai & digital humans: Voice and avatar interfaces that resolve, not deflect — with emotion-aware escalation and full auditability. We run it with named gates, signed baselines and a weekly evidence cadence — the details are below, in the order they happen.

Contact-center chatbots gave conversational AI a bad name: intent trees, deflection metrics and frustrated customers. We build resolution-first assistants — voice and chat agents grounded in your policy corpus, integrated with your CRM, core and telephony stack, measured on resolution and downstream repeat-contact, with emotion-aware escalation to humans and full transcript provenance for compliance.

Digital humans extend the pattern to front-desk scenarios: onboarding in branches, patient intake, training simulation and accessibility interfaces. We deploy them with the same discipline — scripted boundaries, disclosure that the interface is synthetic, consent capture, and fall-back paths — so the experience is engaging without becoming a regulatory liability.

The sectors where Conversational AI & Digital Humans currently runs: Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Retail & Consumer Goods. Each engagement anchors to one named metric in that sector's own language.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Resolution-first design
task-completion architecture measured on resolution and repeat contact, not deflection
Voice stack
streaming ASR, barge-in handling, prosody-aware TTS and telephony integration (SIP/WebRTC)
Grounded dialogue
policy-corpus grounding with citations to source clauses on every answer
Emotion & escalation
sentiment signals that route to humans with context handoff, never cold transfer
Compliance by design
consent capture, synthetic-agent disclosure and transcript retention policies
